topic: Explain quick sort with a pivot on 5, 1, 4, 2, 8, 3
title: Quick Sort and Partitioning

scenes.narration: Quick sort picks a pivot, here the last value of the range. It moves every smaller value before the pivot, which puts the pivot in its final place, then sorts each side the same way.
scenes.caption: Pick a pivot, split around it

scenes.narration: The pivot is 3. The smaller values 1 and 2 move to the front, and 3 lands right after them at index 2, its final place.
scenes.caption: partition all, pivot 3

scenes.narration: Now the left part, 1 and 2. The pivot is 2, and 1 is already smaller, so 2 stays at index 1. Both are in place.
scenes.caption: partition left, pivot 2

scenes.narration: On the right, 5, 8 and 4, the pivot is 4. Nothing is smaller, so 4 swaps to the front of the range.
scenes.caption: partition right, pivot 4

scenes.narration: The last range holds 8 and 5. The pivot is 5, which swaps in front of 8. The array is sorted.
scenes.caption: partition 8 | 5, pivot 5

scenes.narration: Each partition fixed one pivot for good and split the work in two. A bad pivot, like the largest value every time, is what makes the worst case slow.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: The pivot ends in its final place
Smaller values go left, the rest go right
O(n log n) on average, O(n squared) at worst

quiz.question: Quick sort partitions 3, 1, 2 once, using the last value as the pivot. At which index does the pivot end up?
quiz.explanation: Only 1 is smaller than the pivot 2, so 2 ends at index 1.

quiz.question: Quick sort partitions 4, 7, 2, 5 once, with the last value as the pivot. What is the array afterwards?
quiz.explanation: 4 and 2 are smaller than 5 and keep their order; 5 goes right after them.
